title: Polling: one slicer snapshot call for all due projects, skipping parts whose revision did not change
lead: *Proposed.* Drafted 2026-11-11. The daemon's cache reads each project's items, deps and runs with one slicer process per part per project. `slicer snapshot` already reads several projects in one process (`--root` repeats, `--parts items,goals,runs,status,health`) and returns a revision per part. This slice moves the items, runs and goals parts to one `slicer snapshot` call per refresh tick, covering every project that is due, and treats a part whose revision is unchanged as unchanged, so nothing is decoded or broadcast. Freshness stays the same; the number of slicer processes drops from about 3 per project per tick to 1 per tick.
findings_note: Owner 2026-11-11 (feedback from another agent): slicer polling is too frequent and slow. Measured 2026-11-11: each slicer call costs about 100 ms, almost all in slicer's imports (python3 -c pass: 4 ms; import slicer.cli: 77 ms). ork runs slicer list, deps and relay-run list per project, every 5 s when visible, every 1 s for live runs and every 30 s for the other 11 projects.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
*Proposed.* Evidence read on 2026-11-11:

- `Direct.Fetch` (`internal/source/source.go:104-121`) runs one call per part: `Slicer.List` (items), `Slicer.Deps`, `Slicer.Goals`, `Slicer.RelayRuns` (runs), `Adj.Inbox`, `Adj.List`, and `git rev-parse HEAD`.
- Intervals (`internal/cache/cache.go:35-40`, `intervalLocked` at `:162-175`): 5 s for a visible project's parts, 1 s for its Runs part while a run is live, 30 s for the others, and 5 min for goals and decided records. With 12 registered projects this is about 33 slicer processes per 30 s for the hidden ones, plus 3 per 5 s and 1 per second for the visible one with a live run. That is roughly 25-30% of one core spent starting slicer.
- Timings on this machine: `slicer --version` 100 ms, `slicer list --json --lean` 97 ms, `slicer snapshot --json` 153 ms, and `slicer snapshot` with three `--root`s and `--parts items,runs` 142 ms. The venv's `python3 -c pass` takes 4 ms; `-X importtime` shows `import slicer.cli` at 77 ms (`slicer.store` 41 ms, `dataclasses` plus `inspect` about 20 ms). The cost is per process, not per project.
- `slicer snapshot --json` returns `projects[].revision` and `projects[].parts.NAME.revision` beside each part's `value`.
- `deps` is not a snapshot part today (slicer item filed beside this slice). Until it is, Deps stays a per-project call on its own schedule.

Open owner questions (the owner answers before the relay starts):
- Q1 which parts move to the snapshot. (a) items, runs and goals; deps, adj parts and git HEAD stay as they are (recommended). (b) also wait for slicer's deps part and move deps.
- Q2 how a snapshot error is handled. (a) a failed batched call falls back to today's per-part calls for that tick, and one project's `error` in the snapshot marks only that project's parts failed (recommended). (b) a failed call fails every project's parts for that tick.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/source/source.go:104-121` (`Direct.Fetch`; a batched fetch beside it)
- `internal/slicercli` (a `Snapshot(ctx, roots, parts)` call and its types)
- `internal/cache/cache.go` (group due Items, Runs and Goals reads into one batched call per tick; keep each part's schedule; skip `OnChange` when a part's revision is unchanged)
- `internal/cache/cache_test.go`
- `internal/source/source_test.go`
- `testdata/cli/slicer/` (a recorded `slicer snapshot --json` reply)
- `docs/design.md` (dash.refresh)
- `CHANGELOG.md`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Cache: with three projects due at once, one batched fetch is made (a fake fetcher counts calls), not nine part calls.
- Cache: a part whose revision equals the last good read's revision does not call `OnChange` and keeps its value. A changed revision does.
- Source: the recorded `slicer snapshot` reply decodes into the same typed values that `Slicer.List`, `Slicer.RelayRuns` and `Slicer.Goals` give for the same project (a golden comparison).
- Errors per Q2.
- The 1 s live-run refresh still delivers a run state change within one tick.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Wait for Q1 and Q2.
2. Add `slicercli.Snapshot` and its types from the recorded reply. Confirm that its item and run fields carry everything the dashboard reads from `list --json --lean` and `relay-run list`. Record any gap in the slice notes and keep that part per-project.
3. In the cache, collect the due parts per tick and make one batched call. Keep each part's own interval and its `ReadAt`.
4. Compare revisions before decoding. On an unchanged revision, update `ReadAt` only.
5. Docs (*proposed*): `docs/design.md` dash.refresh.
6. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under `## Unreleased` (*proposed*).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go vet ./... && go test ./...` exits 0.
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check --root /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork` and `adj lint` exit 0.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] With the TUI open on a project with a live run, the run's state changes still show within about a second, and `ps` sampling shows far fewer slicer processes than before.
